title: Mexico Picks Up the Pace to Ratify Its New Agreement with the European Union
author: Georgina Saldierna
content:
_This article by[Georgina
Saldierna](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Georgina%20Saldierna) originally
appeared in the [September 22, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/22/politica/mexico-
acelera-el-paso-para-ratificar-su-nuevo-acuerdo-con-la-union-europea),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

The 33rd Meeting of the Mexico-European Union Joint Parliamentary Committee
began this afternoon with a call from Morena and the National Action Party
(PAN) for the executive to **send the Modernized Global Agreement with the
countries of the old continent to the Senate now** , for its ratification.

The Undersecretary of Foreign Affairs, María Teresa Mercado, reported that
both the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs and the Secretariat of Economy are
assembling the file that will be submitted to the upper house, and she
considered invaluable the support that this sovereign body can give to the
document.

Marko Cortés, PAN senator, celebrated that the European Parliament has already
approved the global agreement, while in Mexico, “we are waiting” for it to be
sent for a vote.

**He estimated that it will be endorsed unanimously.**

In the old Xicoténcatl mansion, he called on the Secretary of Foreign Affairs
to carry out the necessary procedures so that the executive does not take any
longer to send it to the Senate for its approval, since after the European
Parliament already endorsed it, he considered that there is nothing more to
review.

Morena senator Alejandro Murat also called for speeding up the work so that
the agreement is presented in the upper house and can be ratified as soon as
possible.

The meeting's work will continue this Wednesday, when strategies to strengthen
economies and value chains will be addressed, as well as to transition toward
sustainable models and turn environmental challenges into opportunities for
shared development, explained Senator Beatriz Robles of the guinda party.
